messages:
Maria: Quick heads-up — running the flashv3 canary on staging surfaced a p90 latency bump for short requests (8-32 tokens). Not huge but reproducible across a few hosts.
Raj: Ack. Can you paste the signal and which model/config? :eyes:
Maria: Using gpt-like-3-small, batch_size=auto, seq_len=32, kv_mode=paged. p90 went from ~42ms to ~60ms on a subset of runs.
Casey: Oof. Any change in kernel selection logs? That sounds like a kernel-choice flip at short seqs.
InfraBot: alert: perf-regression-detected service=runtime env=staging metric=p90_latency delta=+42% hosts=staging-pool-3 link=https://perf.redwood/alerts/1768501234
Maria: Attach few profiling snippets:

```
# nsys summary (truncated)
Kernel: flashv3_fused_attn   calls=12   avg=1.8ms   total=21.6ms
Kernel: flashv3_paged_attn   calls=78   avg=0.4ms   total=31.2ms
Kernel launches increased by ~2.6x
Device memcpy H2D spikes aligned with small batches
```

Maria: The chooser appears to switch to paged path for these shapes and the extra kernel handoffs + memcopies dominate at small sequences.
Sophie: Is this KV cache eviction related? Paged attention touches KV more often, right?
Maria: Yeah — with paged shards we're seeing more KV windowing and extra prefix re-materialization for short tails. Cache hit rate dropped ~8% in the canary trace.
Ben: Do we have a quick mitigation? Maybe prefer fused/fallback kernels for seq<=64 until we fix page overhead.
Raj: I propose a feature flag knob: attn_kernel_selector.short_seq_prefer_fused = true for staging. Roll it for canary and measure.
Casey: Also add a batching tweak: loosen continuous batching threshold for short requests so we don't split them into many tiny kernel calls. That may reduce kernel-launch overhead.
Maria: Plan sketch:
- flip flag in staging: short_seq_prefer_fused=true
- run 1% traffic canary in us-west1 for 1 hour
- monitor p50/p90/p99 latency, KV hit rate, and GPU kernel counts
- abort if p90 regresses >5% or error rate increases

Raj: Commands to flip:

```
# internal flag CLI
redwoodctl flags set attn_kernel_selector.short_seq_prefer_fused true --env=staging
# rollback
redwoodctl flags set attn_kernel_selector.short_seq_prefer_fused false --env=staging
```

Sophie: Add an immediate probe test in perf harness that runs 8/16/32 token beams to validate locally before canary.
Casey: I'll add an automated micro-benchmark that asserts kernel_launchs_per_request < 6 for seq<=32.
Ben: For longer-term — engineering tasks:
- instrument kernel chooser telemetry to expose reasons (latency estimate vs memory estimate)
- profile paged-attn memory access pattern for short sequences
- consider a fast-path fused kernel that avoids rematerializing KV for small prefixes

Maria: Runbook if canary fails:
1) set short_seq_prefer_fused=false (force fused/fallback behavior)
2) scale canary back to 0% traffic
3) collect nsys traces from affected hosts and tag with regression_id
4) revert any batching policy changes

Raj: Who can run the canary? Casey volunteering for 9am PT slot today.
Casey: I can do 9am PT, will co-monitor with Sophie and Ben. I'll post a short status thread when live.
InfraBot: deploy: canary toggled by Casey at 1768504800 (simulated) :rocket:
Maria: Thanks — if this helps others, we should make the short-seq fallback the default for Dedicated customers until we complete kernel-level fixes.
Sophie: Noted. I'll add a short doc in the runbooks repo summarizing the flag and rollback steps.
Ben: Quick note: we saw a related regression earlier but for long sequences when kv-merge was enabled — probably separate but worth cross-referencing (see 1729001111 thread).
Maria: OK closing for now — Casey will update when canary is live. :thumbsup:
